fixes.explanation: That's the number, baker. The LORD says, "My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years." Just a few verses back, Methuselah, Enoch's son, lived 969 years (Genesis 5:27). So 120 is a number you notice right after all those long ones. The verse doesn't say more than what the LORD says here, so I'll leave it right there.
That's the word, baker. "Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth…" This is one of the heavy parts of the passage. The LORD sees it clearly, and the text says so plainly.

Nice word, friend, but it isn't the one in the verse. The text says the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth. That's a heavy thing to read. Wisdom is a good word, but it's not what the LORD sees here.

I can see why you'd pick that, friend, but the text says more than that. It says "…every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time." All the time, not just some of it. So the answer here is False.

You read it right, baker. The text says "…every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time." Not some of the time, all the time. So False is the one that matches the verse.

You've got it, baker. The LORD says, "I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth…" That comes right after the verse where He is grieved in His heart (Genesis 6:6). The text puts the grief and the words side by side.
